answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by issuing each agent a costly, reputation-bound credential earned through periodic peer-graded work. A new identity must first pass a unique task, much like composing a fresh sonnet rather than copying old verses, while its reputation is anchored to a tamper-evident onyx ledger. Other agents randomly audit submissions, making fabricated histories costly to sustain. Like checking a walnut shell before trusting its kernel, the network verifies evidence before granting influence; honest newcomers can still earn trust gradually.
